subject: Oceanography
title: Anatomy of a Wave
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Anatomy of a Wave.

hook.text: Ocean waves move energy across thousands of kilometers—but the water itself barely travels at all.

buildup.text: A wave has a crest (top), trough (bottom), height (vertical distance), and wavelength (crest to crest).

discovery.text: Water particles move in circles as a wave passes—they end up nearly where they started.

twist.text: These orbital motions shrink with depth—below half the wavelength, the water is completely still.

climax.text: So a submarine just 150 meters deep can ride out waves that terrorize ships on the surface.

punchline.text: Waves move energy, not water—the ocean stays put.

quiz.question: What do water particles do as a wave passes?
options: Move in circles and return to roughly the same spot
